name: Design transient git credentials + GitHub integration contract
description:
Produce ONE design document that both implementation steps will follow. Write it to docs/git-remote-credentials.md (project root, docs/ folder). It must specify, with exact file paths and function names read from the code:

A) Transient-credential flow for git remote operations
- Which endpoints change: POST /git/repo/fetch, /git/repo/pull, /git/repo/push (api/codx/junior/api/git.py) and how optional credentials arrive. Prefer a small Pydantic model (e.g. GitCredentialsPayload with username/password) accepted as an OPTIONAL body, kept out of query strings (query strings end up in access logs and the echoed 'command' field).
- How the engine receives them: extend api/codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py so a per-call credential override can be threaded into _token_args()/_run_git() (e.g. _run_git(..., credential=...) or a temporary per-call override) without touching self/settings. Reuse TOKEN_ARG_PREFIX, DEFAULT_TOKEN_USERNAME, TOKEN_VALUE_MASK and _mask_token_args. Support username+password AND token-as-password.
- Structured failure contract: when no credential is configured/used and the failure matches AUTH_ERROR_PATTERNS, the API must answer with a machine readable marker so the UI can prompt. Specify the exact JSON shape and HTTP status (e.g. 401/428 with {"requires_credentials": true, "remote": ..., "hint": ...}) and where it is produced (api/git.py _ensure_success vs git_engine._git_operation_result).
- Security invariants (must be testable): credentials never written to project settings, global git config, credential helper/store, .codx files, logs, audit, error responses or the returned 'command' string; credentials valid for exactly one command invocation; password never echoed back; CISO/redaction helpers (api/codx/junior/security/ciso) already treat the value as a secret.
- Client contract: which component/API module in client/src (repo.js push/fetch/pull at src/api/modules/repo.js:727 and the git view that calls it) shows the dialog, field names, and that the dialog value is never persisted (no store, no localStorage).

B) GitHub integration foundation plan
- Inventory what already exists: api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py (login via GitHubOAuth), api/codx/junior/misc/github.py (issue search), security/user_management.py (GITHUB_ADMINS), and the project PAT in api/codx/junior/settings.py (git_access_token, get/has/masked_git_access_token).
- Propose the minimal feature-flagged foundation: a github settings block on project/global settings (token reference like ${GITHUB_TOKEN}, never a raw secret in .codx), a thin GitHub API client module (list repos, get repo, create/attach remote, clone into the project), and the endpoint surface (paths + models) to list repos and connect a project to a repo. State clearly which parts are implemented in this run and which are left as follow-up.

Acceptance: the file exists, every touchpoint cites a real path:line verified with project_locate/project_read_file, and the JSON contract (credential payload + requires_credentials error) is unambiguous enough for two different workers to implement backend and frontend without asking questions.

**Acceptance criteria**
docs/git-remote-credentials.md exists and contains: touched files list with real paths, the optional credential request model, the requires_credentials error shape, the security invariants as a checklist, and the GitHub foundation plan (implemented vs follow-up).

Make codx-junior ask the user for git username + password (or token) when a remote operation needs credentials and the project settings have none, using them transiently for that single operation only and never storing them (no settings writes, no git credential store, no logs, no task/chat payload).
